_description: Host environment profile for mobile-emulator-setup. Re-read and validated at every invocation by SKILL.md Step 0. Every pinned version, URL, package ID and command the skill uses lives here; SKILL.md names fields, never values.

evidence: react-native-android-setup (#343): the emulator, AVD-home, acceleration, JDK and environment-variable items, verified on Windows in its pilot; copied here as this skill's own items, not shared (#398 decision)
QA #396 (godot-mobile-setup, 2026-11-20): cmdline-tools 23.0 on Windows wraps sdkmanager over the Android CLI; '/' package ids, --list_installed checks

Design-time probes on a Windows 11 host, 2026-11-20, in a scratch tool root with process-scoped variables: sdkmanager installed emulator 37.3.10 and system-images/android-35/google_apis/x86_64; emulator -accel-check reported WHPX installed and usable (exit 0); 'no' piped into avdmanager --% create avd --name <n> --package "system-images;android-35;google_apis;x86_64" --device pixel_6 created the AVD (exit 0) without the platforms package; emulator -avd <n> -no-window -no-audio -no-snapshot-save booted, adb shell getprop sys.boot_completed returned 1 after 60 s, adb emu kill stopped it
android sdk list --all (Android CLI 1.0.16500706, 2026-11-20): system-images/android-35/google_apis/x86_64 and arm64-v8a both listed; avdmanager list device -c lists pixel_6

QA #399 Windows run, 2026-11-20, Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, non-elevated, targets=android, on a fresh tool root (E:/Scratch/qa-399/run1v2) through the host-run harness (Skills/mobile-emulator-setup/tests/host-run/qa-host-run.js): PASS — every item check present and every verify check pass: emulator -accel-check exit 0 with WHPX installed and usable; avdmanager list avd -c listed mobile-emulator-api35 with its .avd folder and .ini under the tool root's Android/avd (ANDROID_AVD_HOME); the headless boot reported sys.boot_completed=1 after 55 s (timeout 300 s), then adb emu kill. tool-folders, android-cmdline-tools, android-sdk-packages, env-android-home (both Path entries), env-android-avd-home and avd-create were applied by the config's own commands and re-checked present. jdk-17, env-java-home and hardware-acceleration are verified by their checks against a JDK 17.0.12, a user JAVA_HOME and WHPX that already existed; their apply commands, and hardware-acceleration's reboot, did not run. The harness stopped emulator processes still running about 1 s after adb emu kill returned.
source._statusNote: status 'verified' means the entry was run and confirmed on that OS through this skill's sequence, with the evidence in source.evidence. toolRoot.question: Where should the Android SDK, the emulator and its system images, the virtual devices (AVDs) and the downloads live? Give an absolute folder path on a drive with room for them (one system image and one AVD take several GB).
toolRoot._noDefault: No default, following react-native-android-setup: a default location is how the system drive fills. Ask on every invocation that has no recorded answer.
toolRoot.normalize: Replace every backslash in the user's answer with a forward slash and strip a trailing slash before deriving paths.

projectAnswers._description: Answers the project's answers file supplies. Read them when present; otherwise ask. They select items through each item's `when`. A template that names this answer gamePlatform (android | ios | both) supplies the same values.

targets.question: Which emulators should this machine run: android, ios or both?

hostKeys.question: Where should the Android SDK, the emulator and its system images, the virtual devices (AVDs) and the downloads live? Give an absolute folder path on a drive with room for them (one system image and one AVD take several GB).

automates: JDK 17 install and the JAVA_HOME user variable, which avdmanager needs (Android)
Android command-line tools, platform-tools, the emulator and one system image under the tool root (Android)
ANDROID_HOME, ANDROID_AVD_HOME and PATH user variables, so AVD data stays under the tool root (Android)
Creating one AVD from the configured device profile and system image (Android)
Emulator hardware acceleration in a separate admin phase: Windows Hypervisor Platform, KVM on Linux (Android)
Verification: acceleration check, AVD listed, a headless boot confirmed by sys.boot_completed, and on macOS an iOS Simulator runtime present, reported pass or fail per check
leavesToUser: Installing Xcode on macOS, and adding an iOS Simulator runtime to it; the skill only reports whether they are present
iOS Simulator on Windows and Linux: it needs macOS with Xcode
Running admin-phase steps (JDK, acceleration) from an elevated shell, and the reboot Windows Hypervisor Platform needs
Opening a new terminal after environment variables change, before creating or starting an AVD
Moving AVDs that already exist outside the tool root

sdkPackages._note: Substitute {packages} with sdkPackages.packages.<os>, each package double-quoted. The id form follows the pinned cmdline-tools archive (QA #396): the Windows and Linux archives (cmdline-tools 23.0) wrap sdkmanager over the Android CLI, whose ids use '/' (cmd splits an unquoted ';' id on Windows); the macOS archive (21.0) is the classic sdkmanager, which takes ';'. The platforms package is not needed to create or boot an AVD (probed 2026-11-20). macOS lists the arm64-v8a image for Apple silicon; an Intel Mac uses the x86_64 image of the same API level and tag.

avd.name: mobile-emulator-api35
avd._note: {avd.name}, {avd.device} and {avd.systemImage} (avd.systemImage.<os>) are substituted into avd-create and the verification. avdmanager is the classic Java tool on every pinned archive and takes the semicolon form; from PowerShell the arguments follow the stop-parsing token so the semicolons reach it (react-native-android-setup lesson 3). It asks whether to create a custom hardware profile; the answer 'no' is piped in.

cmdlineTools._note: Same archives as react-native-android-setup and godot-mobile-setup.

items.summary: The downloads, SDK and AVD folders under the tool root.
A JDK 17. avdmanager is a Java tool and fails without one.
JAVA_HOME as a user variable pointing at the JDK 17 home.
items.valueFrom: The home folder of the JDK 17 that jdk-17 installed or found (the folder containing bin/java), written with forward slashes.

items.summary: The Android command-line tools (sdkmanager, avdmanager) from downloads.cmdlineTools for this OS, unpacked into downloads.cmdlineTools.installLayout.

windows.check: & '{paths.sdk}/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager.bat' --sdk_root='{paths.sdk}' --list_installed; $LASTEXITCODE  # expect exit 0 and a cmdline-tools/latest line; --version exits 1 on cmdline-tools 23.0 even when the tools work (QA #396)

items.summary: platform-tools, the emulator and the system image in sdkPackages.packages for this OS, installed into paths.sdk.
ANDROID_HOME as a user variable pointing at paths.sdk, plus platform-tools (adb) and the emulator folder on PATH.
ANDROID_AVD_HOME as a user variable, so avdmanager writes AVDs under the tool root instead of the user profile on the system drive.
One AVD named avd.name, from avd.device and avd.systemImage for this OS, created in paths.avd. Run from a new terminal so JAVA_HOME and ANDROID_AVD_HOME are set.
Emulator hardware acceleration: Windows Hypervisor Platform (WHPX) on Windows, Hypervisor.framework on macOS, KVM on Linux. The emulator's own accel check reports the result on every OS.

macos.apply: Nothing to install: Hypervisor.framework ships with macOS. If the check fails, report its output.

apply: sudo usermod -aG kvm "$USER"  # takes effect at next login

items.summary: Xcode and its command-line tools. Checked and reported only: installing Xcode is left to the user.

macos.check: xcode-select -p; xcodebuild -version  # expect a developer directory inside Xcode.app and an Xcode version line
macos.apply: Left to the user: install Xcode, open it once to finish its component install, and select it as the active developer directory.

items.summary: An installed iOS Simulator runtime. Checked and reported only: adding a runtime is done in Xcode by the user.

macos.check: xcrun simctl list runtimes  # expect at least one iOS runtime not marked unavailable
macos.apply: Left to the user: add an iOS Simulator runtime through Xcode's platform settings.

verify._description: Run after every apply phase, and on its own when the user asks whether the host is ready. Each check reports pass or fail; the install is verified only when every check that applies passes. Run from a new terminal so the user variables are set.

checks.summary: The emulator finds a usable hardware accelerator.
checks.pass: Exit code 0, and the output names an accelerator as installed and usable (WHPX, HVF or KVM).
avdmanager lists avd.name, and its .avd folder and .ini file are in paths.avd.

checks.summary: The AVD boots headless and Android reports boot completed, then the emulator is stopped.
checks.pass: adb shell getprop sys.boot_completed prints 1 within avd.bootTimeoutSeconds. Report the value and the seconds it took; anything else, or the timeout, is fail.

windows.run: $p = Start-Process "$env:ANDROID_HOME/emulator/emulator.exe" -ArgumentList '-avd','{avd.name}','-no-window','-no-audio','-no-snapshot-save' -PassThru; & "$env:ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb.exe" wait-for-device; $t = 0; do { Start-Sleep -Seconds 5; $t += 5; $b = (& "$env:ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb.exe" shell getprop sys.boot_completed) -join '' } until ($b.Trim() -eq '1' -or $t -ge {avd.bootTimeoutSeconds}); "sys.boot_completed=$($b.Trim()) after ${t}s"; & "$env:ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb.exe" emu kill

macos.run: "$ANDROID_HOME/emulator/emulator" -avd '{avd.name}' -no-window -no-audio -no-snapshot-save & "$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb" wait-for-device; t=0; until [ "$("$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb" shell getprop sys.boot_completed | tr -d '\r')" = 1 ] || [ $t -ge {avd.bootTimeoutSeconds} ]; do sleep 5; t=$((t+5)); done; echo "sys.boot_completed=$("$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb" shell getprop sys.boot_completed | tr -d '\r') after ${t}s"; "$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb" emu kill

linux.run: "$ANDROID_HOME/emulator/emulator" -avd '{avd.name}' -no-window -no-audio -no-snapshot-save & "$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb" wait-for-device; t=0; until [ "$("$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb" shell getprop sys.boot_completed | tr -d '\r')" = 1 ] || [ $t -ge {avd.bootTimeoutSeconds} ]; do sleep 5; t=$((t+5)); done; echo "sys.boot_completed=$("$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb" shell getprop sys.boot_completed | tr -d '\r') after ${t}s"; "$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb" emu kill

checks.summary: On macOS: Xcode is present and at least one iOS Simulator runtime is installed.
checks.pass: xcodebuild -version prints an Xcode version, and xcrun simctl list runtimes lists at least one iOS runtime not marked unavailable. Report both outputs; if either is missing, report what the user has to install.
